data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Filing a sandboxed Python simulation that exactly implements the specified LCG recurrence and face-mapping, returning the six face counts and total plus a calibration trace so the recurrence can be hand-verified before any tally is trusted.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the harness rejects the simulation because a requested_observables key does not resolve in the returned mapping, the proposal yields no evidence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the calibration trace (first ten X_n, die_n pairs) does not byte-match a hand-computed reference from the specification, the implementation is wrong and no tally from it is admissible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the recurrence is not run for the full 10000 terms, the counts are incomplete and the fairness claim is untestable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The generator is X_0=42; X_(n+1)=(1103515245*X_n+12345) mod 2^31; die_n=1+(X_n mod 6). A Python function computes this iteratively for n=1..10000, tallying die_n into six counters. Because 2^31 mod 6=2, the LCG outputs do not cycle through residues mod 6 with perfect uniformity over short horizons, so the exact tallies are only knowable by running the recurrence. The function also emits the first ten (X_n, die_n) pairs as calibration keys (cal_1_x, cal_1_die, ...) so a checker can hand-verify X_1=1103527585, die_1=1, and each subsequent step.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
